alternatives.root_cause: An upstream dependency of fraud-detection became slow and the service waited on it.
alternatives.why_not: The ~1s delay is self-time inside fraud-detection's own process spans with no outbound dependency span, and the service logs the sleep as its own deliberate flagged behaviour.

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value controlling consumer timing was set wrongly.
alternatives.why_not: The change log for fraud-detection is empty over 24 hours, so no configuration file or artifact changed; the switch was runtime-only.

alternatives.root_cause: flagd itself broke and fraud-detection failed on flag evaluation.
alternatives.why_not: No change recorded for flagd, and fraud-detection evaluates the flag successfully — it reports the flag as enabled and then executes the slow path as designed.

verdict.summary: A runtime feature flag served by flagd was enabled for fraud-detection, and the flagged code path inserts a one-second sleep on every consumed order record, stalling consumption from the onset time onward.
verdict.reasoning: Error ratio did not depart from baseline (tr_21c823186d28) — the fault is delay and stalled traffic (8 intervals with no traffic at all), not failures. The service's own logs (tr_d26577bfecc0) show it repeatedly announcing an enabled feature flag and a deliberate one-second sleep per consumed record, and traces (tr_fcc31b75656c) show one trace with ~100 sibling process spans each ~1002ms, matching that injected delay exactly. No deploy or config change was recorded for fraud-detection or for flagd over a full day (tr_cd86f6f11df3, tr_971a82948ecd), which is the signature of a runtime flag flip in the flag store rather than an artifact or file change. Blast radius is limited to fraud-detection and flagd, the flag evaluator, consistent with the flagged path being the failing mechanism. Remediation is to revert the flag value in the flag store.
open_questions: Who flipped the flag and at what exact time — the flag store's own audit trail was not inspected.
Whether upstream producers (the order queue) are backing up and whether any caller-visible errors resulted downstream.
Whether the 8 no-traffic intervals are consumption stall alone or also include a brief restart.
